method: Bounded scan of all ten gana sections of the complete Dhatupatha and Dhatupradipa for explicit Vedic-only or exclusive-use markers, followed by relevant Siddhantakaumudi and Kshiratarangini commentary checks. This is not exhaustive philological certification of every dictionary entry.

confirmed.reason: finite usage not established; nominal restriction

confirmed.exception: kṣi is explicitly licensed in classical language and cited from Kalidasa.

unresolved.finding: Siddhantakaumudi calls the five roots starting dīdhi Vedic. Kshiratarangini editorial remarks and other traditions dispute the extension; vash has explicit classical examples. Dhatupradipa inflects sas/sasti without a Vedic qualifier. No new blanket quarantine proposed.
unresolved.decision: Do not use this disputed group as new hardness supply without direct certification.

unresolved.finding: Siddhantakaumudi reports pṛ/spṛ/smṛ Vedic according to some authorities; Kshiratarangini calls them predominantly Vedic (chandasaprayau), which is not an absolute exclusion.
unresolved.decision: No blanket exclusion from this weaker statement. Avoid using them as fresh hardness leads.

other_gana_sections: No additional explicit whole-group Vedic heading found in Bhvadi, Divadi, Tudadi, Rudhadi, Tanadi, Kryadi or Curadi in this bounded scan. Individual restricted forms and poetic/Vedic exceptions must still be checked.
warning: A dictionary form alone does not license unrestricted classical finite inflection. Absence of a restriction in this bounded scan is not proof of unrestricted usage.
